summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of chronic lymphedema, recurrent cellulitis, obstructive sleep apnea, morbid obesity, and prior DVT/PE on warfarin was admitted for worsening right leg swelling, erythema, pain, and weeping lesions. She had recently improved after a prior admission but experienced a rapid decline. Imaging ruled out DVT but showed significant subcutaneous edema. She was treated with IV clindamycin for cellulitis after an initial dose of vancomycin, and a new PICC line was placed for reliable access. During admission, she was diagnosed with influenza A, likely nosocomial, and treated with oseltamivir. Acute kidney injury resolved with diuresis using IV furosemide, followed by resumption of home Bumex and spironolactone. Her untreated sleep apnea was found to contribute to venous congestion, with overnight oximetry showing desaturations to 70%. INR remained stable on warfarin, and potassium supplements were held due to hyperkalemia. By discharge, infection had resolved, symptoms improved, and she was transitioned to home care with services and detailed follow-up instructions.
problems: Acute on chronic diastolic (congestive) heart failure
Influenza due to other identified influenza virus with other respiratory manifestations
Epilepsy, unspecified, not intractable, without status epilepticus
Morbid (severe) obesity due to excess calories
